PHASE 11 -- ARC CLOSE. Slot 3, the last of the three items left open when phase 9 closed its two named deliverables, and with it the operating-model-v2 arc. DELIVERABLE: check-sourcemap-debugids.mjs no longer inverts under its own failure mode. The old tail read `if (checked === 0) { console.warn('No Sentry-tagged chunks found in the live bundle -- skipping.'); process.exit(0) }`. "No chunk carries a debug-id" is not a reason to skip -- it IS the regression the script exists to catch: debug-ids are injected at build time by @sentry/vite-plugin, so a plugin that is misconfigured, loses its auth token, or is dropped from vite.config.ts ships a bundle with no debug-ids at all, nothing is uploaded, every prod stack trace stays minified, and the guard called that deploy green. It is the debt row that motivated rule R1 in check-script-conventions.mjs (check #63), and the same class as both findings folded into phase 10.2: a guard that reports green when it measured nothing. THE FIX is to stop conflating three different zero-states that `checked === 0` collapsed into one. fetched === 0 (chunk URLs found but not one body readable) means we measured NOTHING and therefore know nothing -- infrastructure, exit 2, R3's code for could-not-measure, never a green. tagged === 0 (bodies read, none carrying a debug-id) is a POSITIVE measurement of a broken build -- exit 1. missing > 0 (tagged chunks whose sourcemap never reached Sentry) fails as before. Only the last of those three used to fail; the middle one, the loudest available evidence of a broken upload, was the skip. Two further honesty fixes fell out of the same reading: the no-token branch exited 0 and now exits 2 (CI sets SOURCEMAP_CHECK_REQUIRE_TOKEN=1 and takes the fail branch above it, so this only changes local runs, where a green on no measurement was the same lie), and a failed fetch of the homepage itself was an unhandled rejection and is now a named exit 2. STRUCTURE follows the shape used throughout slots 1 and 2: network I/O stays in main(), the DECISION is the pure classify({discovered, fetched, tagged, misses}) returning {code, reason, message}, and the canary drives classify() directly, so every verdict is provable without a network. assertMeasured(fetched, MIN_CHUNKS=2) is belt-and-braces on the green path only -- a live bundle always splits into several hashed chunks (vite.config.ts pins five vendor chunks on top of the entry), so a one-chunk sample is evidence we fetched something other than the real app. R4 CANARY: --self-test, 16 cases, every verdict proven in BOTH directions -- the untagged bundle fails AND a single tagged chunk among many untagged still passes (vendor chunks legitimately vary, so the new failure must not fire on a partial tagging); a missing artifact fails AND its detail reaches the message; both could-not-measure states exit 2 AND are diagnosed apart from each other; no zero-measurement state reports success; and the healthy bundle passes, because a guard only ever shown to fail is indistinguishable from one that always fails. Per the rule earned on #189 the canary names its expectations EXPLICITLY -- literal codes and reason strings -- rather than deriving them from classify(), since a spec that derives its expectations from the code under test goes quiet at the same moment the code does. VERIFICATION: 16/16 self-test; a 5-mutation battery in which every mutation was caught by the specs written for it (revert the fix so untagged returns green -> 3 red; downgrade unfetchable to green -> 2; rename the healthy verdict -> 1; disarm the chunk floor to MIN_CHUNKS=0 -> 1; drop the miss detail from the message -> 1), file restored byte-identically after each. NOTE on that battery: M5 first appeared to SURVIVE, and it was the mutation that was broken, not the canary -- the heredoc ate the backslash out of the join('\n') I was matching on, the exact mount trap recorded in the phase 10 ship, so the replace never applied. Rebuilding the escape with chr(92) reproduced it and the spec red-lit correctly. A mutation that does not apply is indistinguishable from a mutation that was caught; verify the mutation landed before believing the guard survived it. WIRING: the canary runs as its own step in sourcemap-check.yml BEFORE the live check, so a broken guard reds there rather than reporting a green it did not earn; it needs no secrets and no network. package.json gains check:sourcemap-debugids and :self-test. Noted while wiring, NOT fixed here: check:image-widths:self-test has no caller anywhere -- a canary nobody runs -- which is a candidate for the ratchet arc below. RATCHET: the R1:empty-sample and R4:no-canary rows for this file are gone from script-conventions-allowlist.json entirely, 106 -> 104 violations across 82 scripts; the ratchet's stale-entry check fired first and named both, which is what re-baselining is meant to feel like. ARC STATE: operating-model-v2 is CLOSED with this ship. All three slots left open at phase 9 have landed -- slot 2 as #188 (80c6b65), slot 1 as #189 (2f66e54), slot 3 here. THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOULD DECIDE THE NEXT ARC, recorded here so it survives the session: 82 guard scripts, 10,730 lines, and only 4 carry a self-test. R4 binds NEW check-*.mjs only, so 78 pre-existing guards are grandfathered and exempt. The recommendation on file is NOT a rebuild -- each of those guards reads as competent, which is exactly why three defects this arc survived reading and fell only to mutation (a scanned>500 floor against a ~900-file corpus, a self-referential corpus claim that went quiet with its own coverage, and a process.exit() truncating 904 lines to 194 on Linux only). The design is fine; the VERIFICATION is missing. The proposal is a canary RATCHET in the shape this repo already runs for rpc-typing-allowlist.json: snapshot the 78 as known debt, let nothing new join (R4 already enforces that), and require any guard you touch to leave the list -- a per-PR tax on code already being edited rather than an unschedulable 78-item project. Authoring pin: claude-opus-5 / high; this session runs claude-opus-5[1m] / high -- effort MATCHES the pin, the [1m] context variant is the only deviation, declared and recorded, not a halt. Worktree C:/tmp/wc-slot3 on branch ci/sourcemap-debugids-guard, cut from origin/main 2f66e54, because a second session holds the main checkout live on ci/upcoming-event-cover-guard. REVIEW FOLD (independent adversarial pass, 5 findings, every one reproduced before folding, all folded as EDITS before commit -- no follow-up commits). TWO of them were this rewrite reproducing, in new clothes, the exact dishonesty class it was written to end. (1) SEVERE: `const arr = lookup.ok ? await lookup.json() : []` turned any non-2xx from Sentry -- an expired token, a missing scope, a 429, an outage -- into an empty artifact list, hence a `misses` entry, hence a confident exit-1 accusation that the sourcemap upload was broken. Reproduced end-to-end against a stubbed 401. An infrastructure fault is exit 2 by this file's own taxonomy, so a non-ok lookup (and a 200 whose body will not parse) now feeds a separate lookupErrors counter and classify() grades it `lookup-unavailable`, code 2, with a message that says in terms this is NOT evidence the upload is broken. (2) SEVERE: only `tagged === 0` failed, so PARTIAL tagging -- the realistic shape of a half-broken @sentry/vite-plugin -- was graded GREEN, and the OK line actively reassured ('all 1 Sentry-tagged chunk(s) have a matching uploaded sourcemap'). Worse, the first canary ENSHRINED it: a case named 'one tagged chunk among many untagged is NOT the untagged verdict' expected 0, justified by a comment claiming vendor chunks 'legitimately vary'. Measuring the live bundle killed that claim -- 73 chunks discovered, 8 of 8 sampled tagged, vendor-react included. The plugin tags the whole build or it is broken, so `tagged < fetched` is now its own exit-1 `partially-tagged` verdict. THE LESSON, and it is the sharper twin of the rule earned on #189: naming expectations explicitly is necessary but NOT sufficient. Every one of those 16 cases was literal, and the canary still passed 16/16 while asserting a bug as intended -- because a case can only catch a defect its author does not already believe in. What broke the tie was measuring the world instead of re-reading the code. Fixtures that encode a claim about reality now say where the number came from. (3) MEDIUM: the MIN_CHUNKS floor ran on the GREEN path only, so a one-chunk page -- a login wall, a CDN error page, exactly what the floor's own comment describes -- was graded as a build verdict ('the plugin did not tag this build'), a confidently wrong accusation, and when the floor did fire its throw mapped to exit 1 rather than 2. The floor now lives INSIDE classify(), ahead of every build verdict, as `sample-too-small` code 2; assertMeasured stays on the green path purely as a backstop should that branch ever stop firing. (4) MEDIUM: MAX_CHUNKS truncates hard -- 73 chunks live, 8 read -- and every message reported the TRUNCATED length as the denominator, so an 11% sample was phrased as if it covered the deploy. `discovered` is now counted before the slice and every verdict states the sample; the OK line says outright that it clears the sample, not every chunk. The canary asserts the population reaches all four messages, and it caught the green one on the first run, which is the pass-direction half of the same overclaim. (5) LOW: the canary drove classify() only, and the Sentry-error branch lives in main(), so it structurally could not reach the branch finding 1 was about. main() is now exported with an injectable `deps.fetch`, and a 6-case plumbing probe drives network -> counters -> classify end to end (healthy, 401, partial, untagged, one-chunk page, unparseable body) -- all 6 correct. VERIFICATION AFTER THE FOLD: 35 self-test cases (up from 16), and a 7-mutation battery in which every mutation was caught by the specs written for it -- revert the untagged fix -> 4 red; grade partial tagging green -> 6; treat lookup errors as misses -> 5; remove the sample floor -> 3; disarm MIN_CHUNKS -> 4; drop the population from the OK message -> 1; make report() swallow the verdict code -> 2. File restored byte-identically after the battery, sha256-verified.
